problems.name: Contains Duplicate
problems.goal: Decide whether a list contains a repeated value; compare the time and memory costs of two approaches.

problems.name: Valid Anagram
problems.goal: Determine whether two strings use the same letters with the same counts, including repeated letters.

problems.name: Two Sum
problems.goal: Find two distinct indices that sum to a target; explain how to improve on checking every pair.

problems.name: Valid Palindrome
problems.goal: Check a phrase for palindrome symmetry while ignoring punctuation and letter case.

problems.name: Two Sum II
problems.goal: Use sorted input to find a target pair and justify why each move can discard candidates.

problems.name: Valid Parentheses
problems.goal: Check whether mixed bracket types close in the correct order; test empty and incomplete input.

problems.name: Binary Search
problems.goal: Locate a target in a sorted array; state an invariant and test absent targets and boundary indices.

problems.name: Min Stack
problems.goal: Design push, pop, top, and minimum queries with constant time per operation, including duplicate minima.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.goal: Choose a buy day before a sell day to maximize one trade; explain the result for falling prices.

problems.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.goal: Find the longest contiguous substring with unique characters; explain how to handle a repeated character.

system_design.name: Delivery framework: requirements and estimation
focus: Separate functional requirements from measurable quality targets.
Explain the sequence from requirements to interfaces, architecture, and deep dives.
Estimate average and peak request rates and storage from explicit assumptions.
Use estimates to justify one design decision rather than calculating everything.
system_design.exercise: Spend 20 minutes reading, 20 minutes framing a daily study notification service, and 10 minutes explaining your requirements and estimates aloud.
system_design.hermes_connection: Use Hermes daily Telegram delivery as the example: define delivery latency, missed-message behavior, and expected traffic.

system_design.name: API design + data modeling: Design a URL Shortener
focus: Specify create-link and redirect APIs, including error cases.
Define the link record, key, expiry, and lookup index.
Explain code uniqueness and collision handling.
Trace a redirect and justify caching and storage choices.
system_design.exercise: Read for 20 minutes, sketch APIs and records for 20 minutes, then defend the redirect path for 15 minutes.
system_design.hermes_connection: Compare stable short-link IDs with the canonical paper URLs Hermes includes in Telegram; distinguish identifiers from delivery records.

system_design.name: Key technologies: cache, queue, load balancer, DB replication
focus: Explain cache placement, invalidation, and stale reads.
Describe how a queue buffers work and how workers acknowledge it.
Explain routing and health checks at a load balancer.
Explain primary/replica writes, replication lag, and failover.
system_design.exercise: Study the building blocks for 25 minutes, draw their request and background-work paths for 20 minutes, and explain a failure in each path for 10 minutes.
system_design.hermes_connection: Start with the current Hermes cron and watchdog; propose when separate queued workers and replicated storage would become useful, without claiming they already exist.

system_design.name: Design a Notification System
focus: Define retries, backoff, and terminal failures.
Explain idempotency when a send succeeds but acknowledgement is lost.
Set provider rate limits and priority handling.
Explain backlog recovery and provider outages.
system_design.exercise: Run a 45-minute mock: 5 minutes requirements, 5 APIs/data, 15 architecture, 15 trade-offs/failures, 5 recap. Then spend 5 minutes scoring your answer.
system_design.hermes_connection: Scale Hermes scheduled Telegram pushes into a multi-user service; use cron stalls and provider failures as concrete failure scenarios.
system_design.access_note: Hello Interview labels the full walkthrough Premium. Use the public prompt for the mock; its free delivery framework and key-technologies pages support the exercise without a login.
